newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to tender for 162,000T corn, soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to tender for 162,000T corn, soybeans.

text.p: Taiwan is expected to tender for up to 108,000 tonnes of corn and 54,000 tonnes of soybeans this week, traders said on Monday.
"Local soybean buyers will finish their September and October purchases this week," a grain trader said.
Taiwan buyers still need to buy 128,000 tonnes of corn and 54,000 tonnes of soybeans to complete their September and October requirements, traders said.
Local buyers last week bought a total of 162,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans for this period.
The Kaohsiung division of Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association on Friday bought 108,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans -- double the amount the market had expected.
A Kaohsiung division buyer said U.S. soybean prices were in an acceptable range.
"U.S. soybeans are at about US$265 to $270 per tonne, which gives us a good profitable margin," he said.
The breakfast association's Taichung division was expected to tender this week to catch up with Kaohsiung, traders said.
Taiwan's CK Group and Members Feed Industry Group may place a major corn tender once the Chicago market gives a clear direction on its next price move, traders said.
"Corn buyers are waiting for the market to show clearly where it is heading," a trader said.
Freight rates from the U.S. Pacific Northwest were quoted at about $11.00 a tonne while rates from the Gulf of Mexico reached $21.50 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized September shipments.
